beats.narration_text: Hej — this is Liam, in for Komal, for Madison's weekly update. Team Madison has four tracks this week. One numbered receipt: SurveyMind — about six hundred three thousand usable responses, code proven on dummy data. Plus Loon Conservatory's first desktop app under test, a small laptop recommendation pilot, and a Ruler-only archetype pipeline.

beats.narration_text: First receipt: SurveyMind. About six hundred three thousand usable human personality responses, loaded and cleaned. Statistical tests check whether two datasets show matching trait patterns. The code was proven first on two synthetic sets: one built to look real — it passed. One built to be wrong — it failed. Next: the real SurveyMind file, not the dummy set.

beats.narration_text: Separately, the laptop recommendation study is a small manual pilot in ChatGPT, using the approved prompts. Real responses are being collected and documented. The review: which brands get recommended, and how that changes when user context is added. Small. Manual. Not last week's runner.

beats.narration_text: The Jungian brand-archetype detector is proving the full pipeline on one seat first: the Ruler, for luxury. Section five is becoming a technical design. Inputs: website copy, social captions, a tagline, maybe competitors. Scoring: real language against the Ruler trait profile, with evidence behind each score — not a black box. Evaluation: a small set of hand-labeled brands, to confirm the tool reads voice, not keywords. One archetype, end to end, before all twelve.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. SurveyMind has a cleaned dataset and code that fails the wrong dummy and passes the right one. Loon's first desktop app is in test. The laptop pilot is collecting. The Ruler pipeline is the design, not twelve detectors. Design judgment: do not report a trait match until the real data runs.
